content: Rides fortnightly between Stratford High Cross and the Bell in Carter Lane
He waters the horses before he turns an inward bag out, and he will carry the letter you wrote, not the one you meant.
He will not carry an instruction in his mouth if it can be written on the paper.
He takes twopence, asks if the news is good, and accepts "just news" without improving it.
He took four lines and twopence, and he would not take the sixty shillings into the pack.
Twopence carries a letter. Nothing in his bag is still an answer, and he will say so.
Eight days come out as dust, dear oats, and no rain, and he does not open the packet.
He will put her letter in no hand but yours, and he keeps a bailiff's twenty apart from an alehouse forty.
He prices houses by what they owe, and he will not move one woman's refusal onto a house he has not been shown.
He prices a road in oats and malt, and this autumn he reads the line back.
He will not take a letter's twopence twice, and he will not hand a wife's letter back across a table.
He reads a list back before he cords, and a shout down the yard is not part of his price.
